fields.description: The status slug as WooCommerce has it, for example processing
fields.label: WooCommerce Status

fields.description: What an order that has this status does in ERPNext. With nothing ticked, its Sales Order only takes the status and lines of the order, and a hold put on it is lifted. Hold, Cancel and Close are done once, when the order gets the status, and so is lifting a hold. The sync makes no Sales Invoices, Payment Entries or Delivery Notes: people make them in ERPNext, and a WooCommerce Order Import for orders first seen completed.
fields.label: When WooCommerce has this status

fields.description: Make the Sales Order of an order first seen with this status, with its Customer, Address and Contact, and submit it. No other action makes one, so without Submit such an order stays out of ERPNext. An order first seen completed is for a WooCommerce Order Import, which also books its payment.
fields.label: Submit

fields.description: Put the Sales Order on hold, once, when the order gets this status. A later status that ticks none of Hold, Cancel, Close and Skip lifts it.
fields.label: Hold

fields.description: Cancel the Sales Order. One that has an invoice, a payment or a delivery, or that is closed, is closed and flagged instead, as the sync never cancels or deletes an invoice. Ticked alone.
fields.label: Cancel

fields.description: Close the Sales Order. Ticked alone.
fields.label: Close

fields.description: Leave the orders with this status out of the hourly sync, as nothing is to be done with them. Ticked alone.
fields.label: Skip

fields.description: Set the WooCommerce Order to this status when the Sales Order reaches this status
fields.label: Push on
